channel.title: If Statements :: CC 210 Textbook
channel.description: The first type of conditional construct we’ll cover is the if statement. This type of statement allows us to build a block of code which will only be executed if the given Boolean expression evaluates to true. Here’s a simple flowchart that shows an if statement as the conditional construct: This flowchart represents a program which will ask the user for a number as input, then print that number as output only if the number is greater than $ 0 $. Then, the program will print Goodbye and terminate. So, if the user inputs -5, the program will only print Goodbye. However, if the user inputs 7, then the program will first print 7 followed by Goodbye. As we can see, the program will execute the section of code that prints the value of the variable if and only if the value of x > 0 is true. Otherwise, it will skip that code and continue with the rest of the program.
